findings.finding: Keyword-only guards classify bare import and network Main extends as unsupported_syntax. Existing passing19 cases do not exercise this malformed-name boundary.
findings.recommendation: Use a non-consuming token-slice guard for identifier (dot identifier)* followed by semicolon for import or opening brace for extends. Reuse identifier/reserved. Preserve cursor, existing diagnostic, source span and primary error order.
findings.resolution: Final name_clause recognizer checks existing token slices without changing cursor; import requires a complete name followed by semicolon and extends requires a complete name followed by opening brace. Five malformed-clause controls added and observed passing.

findings.finding: Override attaches only to existing wildcard lexer failure after a top-level dotted import prefix. Strings/comments are tokenized or skipped before recognition; braces prevent nested import classification. Later lexer failures still precede parser import/extends errors. No grammar acceptance added.
findings.scope_limit: Classifier does not validate material following the first unsupported wildcard; avoid introducing tail lexing or changing failure priority merely to validate an already unsupported construct.
findings.recommendation: Retain unsupported_syntax for import demo.* without trailing semicolon: the primary star already identifies the unsupported wildcard construct from its valid prefix. Do not scan material after the lexer failure or add a comment/whitespace-aware secondary scanner.

findings.finding: Actual registered Model schedules event during initialize. Positive simulation checks committed_events=1 and on_event counter1. Rejection resets counter and asserts0 following prepare_with_registry error. Mutex serializes all counter users. This is meaningful positive-control evidence for event-callback nonexecution, not a claim that initialize itself is never called.

Final tests assert E-0001, reason, prepare stage, source, target/time/event absence, primary, exact half-open coordinates and actual/expected for both ordinary and registered fixtures. Ordinary fixture also asserts complete diagnostic message. Existing leakage/priority controls and five malformed-clause controls meaningfully exercise the narrow contract.
